entries.name: Graph attention network v2
entries.definition: A graph neural architecture whose neighborhood attention scorer applies a learned scalar projection after a nonlinear transformation of the query-neighbor pair, allowing attention rankings to depend on the query node.
entries.identity_notes: GATv2 changes the scoring-function operation order of the original GAT. It is a distinct architecture, not a software version label or a synonym for every graph attention network.
entries.mechanism: Concatenate query and neighbor features, apply a learned affine transformation and LeakyReLU, and then project to an attention score; normalize scores over the neighborhood with softmax and use them to aggregate transformed neighbor features.
entries.locator: Sections 2.2 and 3.3, equations 3–4 and 7 with footnote 5, PDF/printed pp. 3 and 5
limitations: Dynamic attention is an expressiveness property of the parameterized scorer, not a guarantee that any trained instance learns useful node-specific rankings.
This record supports the architecture and operation order, not universal benchmark superiority or a causal interpretation of attention coefficients.

entries.name: Deep Sets
entries.definition: A neural architecture family for unordered collections that combines shared element transformations with symmetric aggregation for invariant outputs, or shared element and pooled-context computations for permutation-equivariant outputs.
entries.identity_notes: Deep Sets denotes the architecture family defined by Zaheer and colleagues, including invariant and equivariant constructions. It is not a synonym for all set functions, PointNet, Set Transformer or graph neural networks.
entries.mechanism: The invariant construction applies a shared neural transformation to each element, sums the transformed representations, and processes the sum with an output network. The equivariant construction combines an element's features with a shared pooled summary using tied parameters, and such layers can be composed.
entries.locator: Sections 2.1–2.2 and 3.1, Theorem 2, Lemma 3 and equation 4, PDF/printed pp. 2–3
limitations: The source's exact set-function representation theorem treats a countable universe; its uncountable-domain discussion establishes a fixed-size case and states a broader conjecture. No unrestricted universality claim is curated.
Permutation invariance and equivariance are different output properties. The selected architecture, aggregation and finite neural representation determine its actual scope.

entries.name: Jumping Knowledge network
entries.definition: A graph neural architecture that sends intermediate node representations from multiple neighborhood-aggregation depths to a final layer-aggregation mechanism.
entries.identity_notes: Jumping Knowledge adds aggregation across layer depths and can be combined with GCN, GraphSAGE or GAT neighborhood operators. It is distinct from ordinary adjacent-layer skip connections and from any one of those base operators.
entries.mechanism: Retain each node's intermediate neighborhood-aggregation representations and combine them at the final stage using concatenation, element-wise maximum, or an LSTM-based attention mechanism over depths.
limitations: Concatenation followed by a node-shared linear transformation is not node-adaptive in its layer weighting; max pooling and the attention variant provide node-dependent selection or weights.
The influence-distribution result is conditional on activation assumptions. No general guarantee of optimal neighborhood range or benchmark superiority is asserted.

The record describes the layer-aggregation family. The paper's attention prose refers to both weighted layer features and weighted bidirectional-LSTM features, so an exact attention implementation would require a separately pinned implementation review.

limitations: The three additions are DRAFT and self-reviewed, not independently approved.
GATv2 expressiveness does not guarantee every trained instance uses dynamic rankings; Deep Sets theorem scope is explicitly bounded; JK concatenation is not universally node-adaptive.
JK attention prose varies between weighted layer and LSTM hidden features; the curated claim stays at the architecture-family level and preserves the implementation uncertainty.
Three distinct concepts were found; the broader frontier is still active.
Public full papers remain local reading aids; exact hashes, locators and access levels are recorded.
